solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plaster head hollow when it's put on

parts.note: a plaster is a dressing for a wound
to head somewhere is to go there

indicators.note: hollow means the inside of the word when is scooped out, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for applying a plaster cast to someone's head, oddly hollowed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plaster' reads as a verb but is the noun, a dressing; 'head' is the verb meaning go. 'hollow' empties WHEN to WN.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe slipped on over nightclothes is a garment one puts on, so the cryptic phrasing defines it by that action.

clue.text: Resolute detectives break up action one way or the other

indicators.note: break up means the detectives split the action word apart from within

parts.words: action one way or the other
parts.note: a deed is an action, and the word reads the same either way
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Determined detectives intervene to stop a fight, whichever side is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Decided and resolute both describe someone firm and unwavering.

clue.text: Online news for everyone? I get a sense of weariness

parts.note: E as in e-mail stands for electronic, online
the plural of new, abbreviated N, gives two Ns
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reading online news meant for everyone finds it tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as plural 'new's, each new being N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weary dissatisfaction with life.

clue.text: Spark is all it takes to make comeback and no end of luck

indicators.note: to make comeback means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: no means that letter is dropped

parts.note: to nick is to steal, to take

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of luck

explanation.surface: A spark of talent is all one needs for a comeback, plus endless luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' gives NICKS; 'no end of luck' drops its K, leaving NICS. 'to make comeback' reverses ALLITNICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or particle, much like a spark of something.

clue.text: Clout round head for this?

parts.note: a clout is a type of short ... with a broad flat round head, and you strike it on its head

explanation.surface: Something you hit hard on its round head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clout' suggests a blow but is also a roofing fastener with a round head.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout nail is a short fastener with a flat round head, and one hits it on the head.

clue.text: Muzzle good foreign article confronting issue

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the first pieces come directly before the last

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
the point at issue is the issue

explanation.surface: Gagging a good foreign piece before it can address an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muzzle' suggests silencing but is the open end of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpoint is the muzzle of a gun, as in being held at gunpoint.

clue.text: Claret possibly poured out for beef

indicators.note: poured out means spoken, as words poured out are uttered

parts.note: claret, red Bordeaux, is an example of wine

explanation.surface: A glass of claret is poured, perhaps to go with roast beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like the meat to pair with claret, but means a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef and to whine both mean to grumble or complain.

clue.text: Spoil dog or beat it

parts.note: milk that spoils is said to turn
to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them

explanation.surface: A choice between pampering the dog or hitting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' and 'beat' suggest treating a dog well or badly; both are verbs with other senses here.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to flee, and beat it is slang for leave quickly.

clue.text: Investigator's rifle

definitions.meaning: a persistent searcher who hunts out facts; the apostrophe s stands for 'is'
to rifle is to search through rummagingly

explanation.surface: A detective's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferret is a diligent searcher, and to ferret about is to rummage through, as one rifles a drawer.

clue.text: In surrender, sappers giving way to senior officer's rank

indicators.note: giving way to says the sappers make room for the officer, one replacing the other

parts.note: rendition is the formal handing over or surrender of something
RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
CO is a commanding officer, the senior officer of a unit

explanation.surface: In a military surrender, engineers stand aside for the rank of a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving way to' swaps RE (Royal Engineers) in RENDITION for CO (commanding officer).
explanation.definitionFit: Condition in the old sense means social standing or station, as in 'people of every condition'.

clue.text: Busy with hip exercise

parts.note: something hip is fashionable, or in
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone is kept busy doing a workout for their hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy line or room is occupied, currently being utilised by someone.

clue.text: Fine diamonds are not broadly speaking variable

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
ain't is the colloquial, dialect form of are not
Y is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A jeweller hedges about whether fine diamonds vary in quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadly speaking' signals the informal speech form AIN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty and fine are synonyms for delicate, small and elegantly made.

clue.text: Minister near retiring — or making head honcho

parts.note: Michael Gove, then the UK Education Secretary

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the abbreviation for near is read backwards

explanation.surface: A government minister about to retire, or perhaps becoming the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was a British Cabinet minister when this appeared. 'retiring' turns NR (near) into RN.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is the person in charge, a colloquial term for the boss or chief.

clue.text: Play departs, having qualified to hold Broadway opening

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: to hold means the word for qualified wraps around the letter

parts.note: someone qualified is able to do a job

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of Broadway

explanation.surface: A theatre production leaves town, having earned a Broadway premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a theatre noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To play at something is to engage casually or superficially, which is what dabbling means.

clue.text: Hippies attend Peel retrospective

parts.note: to attend somewhere is to be at it

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: peel is the skin of fruit

explanation.surface: Former hippies go to a John Peel retrospective.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a BBC DJ famous for championing alternative music.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were the 1950s bohemian forerunners of the 1960s hippies, a loose equivalent.

clue.text: Both sides of Milan having time to socialise

parts.note: Milan's two football clubs are Inter and AC Milan

explanation.surface: Fans of both Milan clubs given time to mix with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both sides' means the two football teams, Inter and AC, not the city's edges M and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to mix and communicate with others, a synonym for being sociable.

clue.text: Queen caught in outpouring of antipathy following European row over British capital

indicators.note: over means placed above in this down entry, so the row comes before British
following means the last piece comes after the others

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: caught in means the queen's letter sits inside the exclamation

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust
R, for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A royal row in Europe sparks an outburst of anti-British hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' is R (Regina) inside UGH, giving URGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.

clue.text: Turn out okay or be an issue from time to time

definitions.text: an issue from time to time

indicators.note: turn out means the letters are rearranged into a different shape

explanation.surface: An exhortation to turn out well or else become a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a problem but means a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearbook is published annually, so it is a recurring edition at intervals.

clue.text: Food kept in dry salt

indicators.note: kept in means one word is held inside the other

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or dry up
fare is food, as in a menu's bill of fare

explanation.surface: Provisions preserved by drying in salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like the preserving agent but is an old sailor, as in 'old salt'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, and a seafarer is one who travels by sea.

clue.text: Head of security too flipping close to cardinal for comfort

indicators.note: close to means placed right beside, so the cardinal's letters come next
head of means the first letter of security
flipping means the word too is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: HE, His Eminence, the title of a cardinal

explanation.surface: The security chief is much too close to the cardinal for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but reverses TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone is to comfort or console them.

clue.text: Face increase in sort of web access

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
to up something is to increase it

explanation.surface: A face shows growing interest in a kind of internet connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dial-up was the early internet connection made through a telephone modem.

clue.text: Roast duck before work at show

indicators.note: before means the earlier pieces precede the last

parts.note: to roast is to criticise harshly, to pan
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, O
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Cooking roast duck ahead of a culinary show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast duck' suggests dinner; both words have other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoply is a splendid display, an impressive show.

clue.text: More vino ordered for one who indulges to the full

definitions.text: one who indulges to the full

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone orders more wine, a person who indulges to the full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like asking a waiter but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats everything, so the term extends to anyone who takes in all on offer.

clue.text: Solid reviews to some extent backed composer

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Firm critical praise, partly supporting a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of operas such as Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Sprite and chocolate bar with no wrapper left out

indicators.note: out means this letter is removed
with no wrapper means the outer letters are stripped away like a wrapping

parts.note: Toblerone is a triangular chocolate bar

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink and a chocolate bar, unwrapped, are left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprite' suggests the soft drink but is a fairy. 'with no wrapper' takes T and E off TOBLERONE; 'out' then removes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, a fairy being a sprite.

clue.text: Diminutive Cabinet Minister runs half-marathon

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: half means the back half of marathon is taken

explanation.surface: A short Cabinet minister runs a half-marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' looks like small stature but means abbreviated: Rt Hon, Right Honourable, the title of Privy Counsellors.
explanation.definitionFit: Right Honourable is the title of Cabinet ministers, shortened in writing to two abbreviations.

clue.text: Rain down off and on before long

indicators.note: off and on means every other letter is used

explanation.surface: Rain falls intermittently, soon to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon, shortly.

clue.text: One rambling tramp at side of road

parts.note: a tramp is a long walk, a hike

indicators.note: side of means one edge of the word road, here its first letter

explanation.surface: A tramp, wandering along the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' suggests a vagrant but is the noun for a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling in Britain is walking in the countryside for pleasure, as hikers do.

clue.text: Right of possession for Onassis, perhaps, doing East-West trade

indicators.note: doing East-West trade means the left-hand and right-hand parts of the word swap places

parts.note: Aristotle Onassis was a famous Greek shipping magnate

explanation.surface: Onassis claims rights over goods traded between East and West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing East-West trade' swaps the two halves of SHIPOWNER, putting SHIP at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the legal right to hold and control property.

clue.text: Luxury is cash to cover Silk Cut plus tip on horses

indicators.note: to cover means money wraps around the other letters

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: cut means the word Silk loses a letter, its first

parts.note: plus means and

indicators.note: tip on means the first letter of horses

explanation.surface: A gambler's indulgence: money for Silk Cut cigarettes and a racing tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Silk Cut is a British cigarette brand, so the surface reads as shopping; 'Cut' is really the instruction to drop the S. 'to cover' puts the cash around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A land of milk and honey is proverbial for abundance and ease, hence luxury.
